answer.rationale: Rollback is off the table (compliance-mandated security patch), so memory_b1 doesn't apply. The symptom is write-path latency under peak settlement load, which matches the capacity/headroom pattern in memory_b3 — provisioning ahead of heavy write traffic kept queues flat. Regional failover (memory_b2) is riskier during peak writes because shifting live write traffic mid-peak could lose or duplicate in-flight customer writes, violating the primary objective; I want to verify its archived record before ruling it out entirely. Circuit breakers target a failing partner dependency (no evidence of one here), and read replicas offload reads, not the write path. Adding capacity is reversible, preserves all writes, and directly addresses latency under load.
